answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that a payout needs signatures from several agents who never traded with each other, so one operator cannot self-attest a ring. The checking is done by agents who gain nothing from waving it through. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a bridge of small steps that each agent re-checks. Read it as a ledge of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check. Think of the atlas instead of a gate, built one verified layer at a time.
